title: The September Epsilon Perseid meteor shower peaks overnight. Here's how to watch
excerpt: The American Meteor Society considers it a “minor” meteor shower.
content:
The American Meteor Society considers it a "minor" meteor shower.

By Briana Trujillo • Published September 9, 2026 • Updated on September 9, 2026 at 4:47 pm

Subscribe to our YouTube channel! NBC6 South Florida

The Epsilon Perseids peak Wednesday night into early Thursday morning. The American Meteor Society considers it a "minor" meteor shower.

Steve Luxenberg, president of the South Florida Amateur Astronomers Association (SFAAA), said this shower occurs at around midnight, and that at best, "only a few meteors are visible per hour."

But if you've decided you want to see them, face northeast from a dark location away from city lights.

"Observing meteor showers requires no telescope, only a chair, bug spray, and patience. Always know where you are going, don’t travel alone, [and] safety is the most important rule," Luxenberg advises.
